accepted.s: Which one of the following programmes was launched through collaboration between CSIR and Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan in 2017?
accepted.x: JIGYASA was started through CSIR–Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan collaboration in 2017.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme from its partner bodies and launch year.
accepted.sec: Student-scientist and hackathon programmes → partner bodies and objective

accepted.s: The primary objective of JIGYASA is to
o: create a network of science clubs across India
help ministries frame national technology missions
connect Kendriya Vidyalaya students with CSIR laboratories
accepted.x: JIGYASA is intended to establish a student–scientist connect by taking Kendriya Vidyalaya students into CSIR laboratories.
accepted.tq: Match the programme objective with its direct beneficiary.
accepted.sec: Student-scientist and hackathon programmes → partner bodies and objective

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Smart India Hackathon:
1. It is associated with the Innovation Cell of the Ministry of Education.
2. AICTE has been a partner from 2017.
3. It enables students to solve problems posed by ministries and industry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Smart India Hackathon is partnered by the Ministry of Education’s Innovation Cell and AICTE and addresses problems posed by ministries and industry.
accepted.tq: Test all partner and objective statements before selecting the comprehensive combination.
accepted.sec: Student-scientist and hackathon programmes → partner bodies and objective

accepted.s: VIPNET is associated with which of the following objectives?
o: Establishing a network of science clubs across India
accepted.x: VIPNET, associated with Vigyan Prasar, aims to build a network of science clubs across India.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation–objective association to distinguish closely related programmes.
accepted.sec: Student-scientist and hackathon programmes → partner bodies and objective

accepted.s: The National Supercomputing Mission was launched in which year?
accepted.x: The National Supercomputing Mission was launched in 2015.
accepted.tq: Separate the mission’s launch year from the years of individual PARAM systems.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: The National Supercomputing Mission is jointly associated with which two organisations as its principal ministries or departments?
accepted.x: NSM is associated with the Department of Science and Technology and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who runs the mission?’ test to distinguish the responsible bodies.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: The National Supercomputing Mission is implemented by
accepted.x: NSM is implemented by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru.
accepted.tq: Distinguish implementing institutions from the ministries associated with the mission.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the first National Supercomputing Mission system?
accepted.x: PARAM Shivay was the first NSM system, established in 2019.
accepted.tq: Use the first-in-series clue to identify the earliest PARAM system.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (PARAM system)
A. PARAM Shivay
B. PARAM Brahma
C. PARAM Pravega
D. PARAM Ganga
List-II (Host institute)
1. IISER Pune
2. IIT Roorkee
3. IIT (BHU) Varanasi

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: PARAM Brahma is hosted by IISER Pune, not IISc Bengaluru. PARAM Pravega is associated with IISc Bengaluru.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped host institute in the PARAM-system list.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: PARAM Shakti was associated with which of the following institutions in 2019?
accepted.x: PARAM Shakti was associated with IIT Kharagpur in 2019. A separate 3.1-petaflop PARAM Shakti system was also launched at IIT Madras on C-DAC RUDRA servers.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the institution linked to the 2019 system and the later IIT Madras installation.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: The PARAM Shakti system launched at IIT Madras was described as a
o: 25-hub cyber-physical system hosted by IIT Kharagpur
50-qubit quantum computer hosted by IISER Pune
accepted.x: MeitY launched a 3.1-petaflop PARAM Shakti system at IIT Madras on C-DAC RUDRA servers.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive capacity and server platform with the correct system.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Quantum Mission:
1. Its outlay is ₹6,003.65 crore.
2. It is implemented over eight years.
3. Its goal includes developing intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50 to 1,000 physical qubits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The National Quantum Mission has an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for eight years and targets intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50–1,000 physical qubits.
accepted.tq: Check the figure, duration and technical range together.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: Which organisation is identified with the National Quantum Mission?
accepted.x: The Department of Science and Technology is associated with the National Quantum Mission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the nodal science ministry from partner bodies of student programmes.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional structure of NM-ICPS?
o: 10 Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads established as statutory bodies
25 Technology Innovation Hubs established as Section-8 companies in host institutes
25 science clubs established exclusively in Kendriya Vidyalayas
accepted.x: NM-ICPS provides for 25 Technology Innovation Hubs, constituted as Section-8 companies in host institutes.
accepted.tq: Use the composition and legal form to identify the correct institutional arrangement.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a technology vertical mentioned in connection with the NM-ICPS hubs?
accepted.x: The listed NM-ICPS technology verticals include AI/ML, robotics, cyber security and quantum technologies. Agricultural marketing is not listed among them.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated set of technology verticals.
accepted.sec: National technology missions - NSM (PARAM systems), NQM, NM-ICPS

accepted.s: The NM-ICPS Technology Innovation Hub associated with IISER Tirupati focuses on
accepted.x: The IISER Tirupati TIH, IITTNiF, is associated with Positioning and Precision Technologies.

accepted.s: Atal Innovation Mission is a flagship initiative of
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
accepted.x: Atal Innovation Mission is a flagship initiative of NITI Aayog.

accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s: Atal Innovation Mission was set up in 2016, although it was announced in which Union Budget year?
accepted.x: AIM was announced in the 2015 Budget and set up in 2016.
accepted.tq: Separate announcement year from establishment year.
accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the components of Atal Innovation Mission:
1. Atal Tinkering Labs are intended for schools and cover grades 6–12.
2. Atal Incubation Centres support start-ups in universities and institutions.
3. Atal Community Innovation Centres focus on rural and under-served areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the respective AIM components.
accepted.tq: Match each component with its target group and setting.
accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s: Atal Tinkering Labs primarily expose students to which combination of areas?
o: Quantum cryptography, satellites and marine biology
Only coding and conventional laboratory chemistry
accepted.x: ATLs in schools introduce students to areas such as the Internet of Things, 3D printing and robotics.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete technology cluster associated with ATLs.
accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Atal New India Challenges — school grades 6–12 only
accepted.x: ARISE stands for Atal Research and Innovation for Small Enterprises and is associated with MSMEs. AICs support start-ups, ACICs focus on under-served areas, and Atal New India Challenges address national challenges.
accepted.tq: Use the component’s target sector to reject neighbouring AIM components.
accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s: Atal New India Challenges are intended to promote
o: the appointment of innovation mentors in Andhra Pradesh
only the expansion of science clubs
accepted.x: Atal New India Challenges focus on product innovation directed towards national challenges.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a challenge-based innovation component from incubation and laboratory components.
accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes AIM 2.0?
o: It was launched in 2024 and continues till March 2028 with an allocation of ₹2,750 crore.
It was launched in 2018 and funds only NM-ICPS hubs.
It was launched in 2016 and continues for eight years with an allocation of ₹6,003.65 crore.
It was launched in 2025 and continues till March 2027 with an allocation of ₹1 lakh crore.
accepted.x: AIM 2.0 was launched in 2024, has a period up to March 2028 and an allocation of ₹2,750 crore.
accepted.tq: Match the launch year, end date and allocation as one factual unit.
accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s:
Consider the following components or targets of AIM 2.0:
1. LIPI, involving 30 vernacular innovation centres in 22 scheduled languages
2. 2,500 new Atal Tinkering Labs
3. 10 Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads
4. Deeptech Reactor
Which of the above are associated with AIM 2.0?
accepted.x: LIPI, 2,500 new ATLs, 10 Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads and the Deeptech Reactor are all associated with AIM 2.0.
accepted.tq: Prefer the comprehensive option when every listed component belongs to the same initiative.
accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s: Which State was identified as the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0?
accepted.x: Tripura was identified as the first State Innovation Mission under AIM 2.0.
accepted.tq: Use the first-in-series fact to distinguish the state from other innovation leaders.
accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.sec: Atal Innovation Mission - parent body and components

accepted.s: The Ratan Tata Innovation Hub operates under which policy and is linked with which seed fund?
o: National Quantum Mission and ₹6,003.65-crore Quantum Fund
AP Startup Policy 2015–20 and ₹500-crore ATL Fund
AP Innovation & Startup Policy 2024–29 and ₹22-crore RTIH–SIDBI Seed Fund
accepted.x: RTIH functions under the AP Innovation & Startup Policy 2024–29 and is linked with the ₹22-crore RTIH–SIDBI Seed Fund.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the RDI Scheme:
1. It was approved by the Cabinet on 1 July 2025.
2. It provides ₹1 lakh crore over six years.
3. ₹20,000 crore is earmarked for 2025–26.
4. It is steered by the Governing Board of ANRF, with DST as the nodal department.

First State Innovation Mission — Andhra Pradesh; first NSM system — PARAM Shakti
